prompt: Mark the lines in this cold email that will hurt the reply rate.

task.prompt: Mark the lines in this cold email that will hurt the reply rate.

segments.text: Subject: PARTNERSHIP OPPORTUNITY!!! Best app developers in the world
segments.issue: All-caps, exclamation marks and hype look like spam and trigger filters.

segments.text: Hi Tom, saw your team launched same-day prescription delivery last month.
We are a 150-person agency founded in 2012 with offices in four countries and 400 happy clients across every industry.
segments.issue: A paragraph about yourself instead of the prospect; nothing here is relevant to Tom.

segments.text: Teams scaling delivery often hit driver-dispatch bottlenecks; we built a dispatch app that cut a pharmacy client's late orders by a third.
Worth a 15-minute chat next week to see if that applies to you?
Please see our attached 30-page company brochure and price list.
segments.issue: Large attachments in a first email hurt deliverability and ask too much of a cold reader.

prompt: Rank these cold email subject lines for a VP Operations at a delivery startup, best first.

task.prompt: Rank these cold email subject lines for a VP Operations at a delivery startup, best first.

items.label: Late deliveries since the same-day launch?

task.explanation: A short, specific subject tied to their situation wins; a personal but vague one is next; a generic pitch is weak; hype and urgency look like spam.

prompt: You are launching a cold email campaign to 300 health-tech founders from a freshly bought list.

task.prompt: You are launching a cold email campaign to 300 health-tech founders from a freshly bought list.

steps.question: What should happen before sending?
options: Add every founder to the CC line of one email
Send to everyone twice to be safe
Send all 300 today from the main company domain
Verify the emails, use a warmed-up sending domain, and start with small daily volumes
steps.explanation: Verification and gradual volume protect deliverability and the main domain's reputation.

steps.question: How should you personalise at this scale?
options: Only swap in the first name
Segment by a shared situation and add one specific line per prospect for the top accounts
Write 300 entirely unique essays
Skip personalisation
steps.explanation: Segment-level relevance plus targeted custom lines balances quality and time.

steps.question: Bounces hit 9% after the first batch. What do you do?
options: Switch to a new domain and send more
Remove the unsubscribe link
Keep sending
Pause, clean the list, and re-verify before continuing
steps.explanation: High bounces damage sender reputation; stop and fix the data first.

prompt: Write a cold email (subject line plus body) to this prospect.

task.prompt: Write a cold email (subject line plus body) to this prospect.
task.context: Prospect: Maya Chen, Head of Operations at a 60-clinic physiotherapy chain. Trigger: they just posted three receptionist job ads and their reviews mention long phone hold times for booking. Your agency has built online booking and reminder apps for clinic groups; one past client cut no-shows by 30%. Goal: a short call.

rubric.label: Relevant opening
rubric.description: Opens with a specific observation about Maya's situation (hiring, hold times), not about the agency.

rubric.label: Clear value and proof
rubric.description: Links the problem to a concrete outcome with brief, credible proof (the no-show result).

rubric.label: Low-friction CTA
rubric.description: Ends with one simple, easy-to-answer ask such as a short call or interest check.

rubric.label: Short and skimmable
rubric.description: Subject is short and specific; body is a few short sentences with no jargon or hype.

task.sampleAnswer:
Subject: Booking calls at your clinics

Hi Maya, I noticed you're hiring three receptionists, and a few recent reviews mention long holds when booking. That usually means the phone is doing the job an online booking flow could.

We built booking and reminder apps for clinic groups; one cut no-shows by 30% and freed front-desk time for patients in the room.

Would a 15-minute call next week to see if the same approach fits your 60 clinics be useful? If not, no worries.

Best,
Sam

prompt: Order the parts of a strong cold email body, top to bottom.

task.prompt: Order the parts of a strong cold email body, top to bottom.

items.label: Brief proof of how you solved it for someone similar
One clear, low-effort call to action
A specific observation about the prospect

task.explanation: Relevance earns attention, the problem earns interest, proof earns credibility, and a single ask makes replying easy.

prompt: Two email variants were A/B tested. Work out the reply rate and the meetings per 100 delivered emails for each, then decide which drove more meetings.

task.prompt: Two email variants were A/B tested. Work out the reply rate and the meetings per 100 delivered emails for each, then decide which drove more meetings.
task.explanation: A: 24/400 = 6%, 8/4 = 2 meetings per 100. B: 36/400 = 9%, 6/4 = 1.5. B gets more replies but A books more meetings, which is the real goal.

prompt: A prospect replies to your cold email: "Not interested, we have an in-house team."

task.prompt: A prospect replies to your cold email: "Not interested, we have an in-house team."

steps.question: What is the best reply?
options: Ignore and keep the sequence running
Send a discount offer
Argue that agencies are always better
Thank them, acknowledge the in-house team, and offer a narrow, useful angle (e.g. overflow or a specialist piece) with no pressure
steps.explanation: Respect the answer, leave one relevant door open, and keep it short.

steps.question: What happens to the automated sequence?
options: It keeps sending the remaining steps
Stop it for this contact immediately
Restart it next week
Add them to a second sequence
steps.explanation: Continuing to email someone who said no damages reputation and may breach consent rules.

steps.question: How do you record this in the CRM?
options: Mark as qualified
Leave it untouched
Delete the contact
Mark the reason (in-house team) and set a sensible re-engagement date if appropriate
steps.explanation: Logging the reason keeps data useful and allows a respectful revisit later.

prompt: What is the main job of a cold email's first line?

options: State the price
Introduce the agency's history
Show the prospect it is about them and worth reading on
List all services
mcq.explanation: The first line, often shown as a preview, decides whether the rest gets read.

prompt: Why is a single call to action better than offering several options in a cold email?

options: It shortens the email to fit filters
It reduces the effort of deciding, which raises the chance of a reply
Multiple links are illegal
It hides the unsubscribe link
mcq.explanation: One clear, low-effort ask is easier to say yes to than a menu of choices.

prompt: Open rates look strong but replies are near zero. What is the most likely issue?

options: The body or offer is not relevant enough to the recipients
The subject line is too good
The list is too small
Deliverability is failing
mcq.explanation: Opens show the email arrived and the subject worked; weak replies point to the message, offer or targeting. Note that opens can also be inflated by privacy features, so treat them as a rough signal.
